title: One Repo, One Product
objective: After this lesson you will be able to lay out a full-stack agent repo (api/web/shared), draw versioned contract boundaries between halves, and decide what lives where with the second-consumer test.
why: Full-stack agents die in the seams: frontend/backend drift, unversioned event shapes, auth as an afterthought, threads owned by nobody. One repo with contracted boundaries makes the seams explicit and evolvable — halves deploy independently behind versions instead of coordinating every change in meetings.

blocks.text: **api/** (Spring Boot: controllers, ChatClient beans, tools, persistence), **web/** (React: chat UI, streaming client, thread views), **shared/** (OpenAPI spec, SSE event shapes, DTO JSON schemas — versioned). Shared owns every cross-half assumption: event names, entity shapes, error envelopes. Halves import shared; never each other's internals.

blocks.caption: Versioned event shapes: additive freely, breaking with deprecation

blocks.text: Placement rule: would a *second, different consumer* use this? SSE parsing, auth headers, retry budgets → shared libraries. Store-specific prompts, brand copy → respective halves. Shared code without two consumers is premature abstraction — duplicate twice, extract on the third use with evidence.

blocks.title: Version the boundary
blocks.note: Run it: expect true,true,false,true. Old clients tolerate new servers (ignore unknown frames); new clients refuse old servers (missing frames they need). Compatibility is directional — test both directions.

items: api/web/shared layout with versioned contracts (OpenAPI + event shapes) as the only cross-half coupling
Second-consumer test places shared code; duplicate twice before extracting
Additive evolution freely; breaking changes versioned with deprecation windows

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice compatibility matrix and explain the single false. (b) Place five items (SSE parser, brand copy, auth headers, triage prompt, retry budgets) via the second-consumer test. (c) State the deprecation policy for removing an event frame (notice, window, proof).
hints: False case: v2 client + v1 server (needs frames the server never sends). Directional compatibility proven.
Shared: SSE parser, auth headers, retry budgets (multi-consumer). Halves: brand copy (web), triage prompt (api domain).
Deprecation: announce + dual-serve window + zero-usage proof from logs before removal.
exercise.why: Directional compatibility (tolerance one way only), placement by second-consumer evidence, and deprecation with usage proof are the three boundary judgments.
exercise.code: // Boundary pattern: versioned contracts + tolerance direction + deprecation proof.

quiz.q: Frontend imports backend internals directly. Problem + fix?
options: Unversioned coupling: every backend change risks UI — route through shared versioned contracts
quiz.explain: Cross-half imports bypass versioning: changes propagate untested. Shared contracts version the seam.

quiz.q: v2 client against v1 server. Expected?
options: Refuses: new clients need frames old servers never send — compatibility is directional
quiz.explain: Old-tolerates-new (ignore unknowns); new-requires-new. Directionality tested both ways, never assumed symmetric.

quiz.q: Removing an SSE frame next week. Process?
options: Announce + dual-serve window + zero-usage log proof → remove (deprecation with evidence)
quiz.explain: Removals need notice, overlap, and proof of disuse. Unused-frame claims require log evidence, not belief.

summary: api/web/shared with versioned contracts; second-consumer placement; additive freely, breaking with deprecation proof. Seams explicit and evolvable.
next: Boundaries drawn — now the backend surface: controllers, SSE streaming, and validated tool endpoints. Next: Boot API design.
